# APOLOGETIC PREFACE,
<note>original: "PRÆFATIO APOLOGETICA." In the 16th and 17th centuries, an "apology" was not an admission of guilt, but a formal academic defense or justification of one's teachings against potential detractors.</note>
->That is<-
## Short PREFACE of Protection and Defense.

<image-desc>Two rows of decorative typographical fleurons arranged in a horizontal band.</image-desc>

GOD’S grace and blessing be upon the kindhearted reader: But especially to each and every faithful lover of the universal, <note>original German: "Catholischen." Khunrath uses the term in its original Greek sense of *katholikos*, meaning "universal" or "all-encompassing," referring to a truth that applies to the entire natural world rather than a specific church denomination.</note> invincible Truth that conforms to Nature; I wish to see and receive the LIGHT of NATURE, <note>The "Light of Nature" (*Lumen Naturae*) is a concept made famous by the physician Paracelsus. It refers to the divine wisdom or "spark" hidden within the physical world, which a philosopher can learn to "read" through observation and alchemy.</note> in your LIGHT, O GOD! You who are a LIGHT in whom there is no darkness, AMEN.

---

<margin>
Whether it is. <note>original Greek and Latin: "ὅτι ἐστὶ / an sit."</note>
What and why it is. <note>original Greek and Latin: "Διότι ἐστὶ / Quid & quare sit." These are standard logical categories used by scholars to structure an argument: first proving a thing exists, then explaining its essence and cause.</note>
</margin>

Rightly, concerning every thing, one asks first and foremost: **WHETHER IT IS**, and afterwards, **WHAT IT IS.**

<summary>Heinrich Khunrath opens his preface by invoking the "Light of Nature" and dedicating his work to those who seek universal, natural truth. He begins his formal defense by stating that one must first establish the existence of a thing before discussing its nature.</summary>

# PREFACE.

<margin>
With Indisputable Demonstrations. <note>original Latin: "Demonstrationibus Apodicticis." In logic, an apodictic proof is one that is absolutely certain and necessary, rather than merely probable.</note>
</margin>
That the admirable Philosophers’ Stone <note>original Latin: "LAPIS Philosophorum." The legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and granting longevity or spiritual perfection.</note>—the wonderful **STONE** of the Wise—exists within the *Nature of Things* <note>original Latin: "Rerum NATURA."</note> has been sufficiently demonstrated and proven with infallible and diamond-like foundations in the Third Figure of my **AMPHITHEATRE OF ETERNAL WISDOM**, etc. And the number seven is by no means a number of lies (as the father of all lies <note>A reference to the Devil, though Khunrath is specifically targeting his academic and theological critics here.</note> blasphemously speaks through his lying mouths, claiming that he who speaks of seven loves to lie).

<margin>
Concerning the MYSTERIES of the SEVEN, see chapter 10, book 2, of *On Occult Philosophy* by H. C. Agrippa. <note>Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa (1486–1535) was a famous occultist and polymath. His *De Occulta Philosophia* was a foundational text for Renaissance magic and the study of the hidden properties of numbers (numerology).</note>
</margin>
But rather, it is a holy number (according to the teaching of the Spirit of all truth, both in Holy Biblical scripture and also in the Great-Worldly <note>Khunrath refers to the "Macrocosm" or the physical universe as a book written by God.</note> as well as the **GOD**-Natural writings), full of divine mysteries and the steadfast truth of natural secrets. This is the truth which the desperate arch-blasphemer, through his mockery and blasphemous words mentioned shortly before, seeks to make suspiciously evil.

Trincunria <note>Likely referring to Claudio Albagini, an author who wrote on the "concord" or agreement of medical authorities.</note> (page 80 of *On the Concord of Physicians*), that since a conceptual definition <note>original Greek: ἐννοηματική (ennoymatike). This is established through the testimonies of many good philosophical writings; through (Praise **God**!) unwavering reason; through the **Cabalistic** <note>Referring to Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that Renaissance thinkers like Khunrath adapted into "Christian Cabala" to find hidden meanings in nature and scripture.</note> traditions of experienced people; and partly also through the confirmation of my own practice—both theosophical in the **ORATORY** <note>original: "ORATORIO." Khunrath famously argued that the alchemist must balance prayer with manual work.</note>. Thus, from the true foundation of the **LIGHT of NATURE**, it is not only **TRUE**, but also, so far as the properties of Divine and Natural mysteries in the current...

<meta>This page continues Khunrath’s address to the reader, following his assertion that he has provided the "conceptual definition" of the Philosophers' Stone that previous sages withheld. # PREFACE.

<margin>
They [the ancient philosophers], if they had wished, could have explained it. I have explained it.

Now the conceptual <note>original Greek: ἐννόηματική (ennoymatike)</note> definition, which you rightly call the door and vestibule of this entire notion, will teach you what you seek: **that it exists** <note>original Greek: ὅτι ἔστι (hoti esti), a philosophical term referring to the existence of a thing rather than its essence.</note>, if only you are attentive.

Synoptically, Catholically <note>In this context, "Catholic" is used in its original sense of "universal" or "all-encompassing," rather than referring to a specific church.</note>, briefly summarized, Universal or General.
</margin>

...to bring forth to the public light of the perverted world / to permit it / to give it forth **CLEARLY**. Since I therein diligently and faithfully bring to light the **Catholic** or **Universal Natural CHAOS** of **Nature-conforming Alchemy** <note>original: "Alchymiæ"</note> and of the **Alchemists**; in which the **SALT of Wisdom**, **Macrocosmic** <note>original: "Großweltlich," referring to the great world or the universe as a whole.</note>, **Physical** or **Material**, dwells according to its **Catholic** or **Universal NATURAL Substance** and essence; together with **AZOTH** <note>A term for the universal solvent or the essential spirit of mercury.</note>, **HYLE** <note>original Greek: ὕλη (hyle), referring to primordial matter or the fundamental substance of the universe.</note>, or the **MATTER of the WORLD / FIRST MATTER** <note>original: "Materia Mundi / Prima"</note>, the first created matter of the world’s beginning, along with all material things therein—that is, the **MERCURY of the Sages**. Likewise, the **Conditions** or **circumstances** of the **MAGNESIA** <note>In alchemy, Magnesia refers to the "mother" or the crude material from which the Stone is extracted.</note>—namely, the **SUBJECT** and true **MATTER** of the **Universal** and therefore the **GREAT STONE** of the Sages and lovers of Wisdom—are shown here in detail.

# PREFACE.

<margin>Various people's judgments of my writings.</margin>
I know well that various and many strange judgments <note>original Latin: *judicia*</note> of these my recently mentioned **Works** <note>original Latin: *Operibus*</note> have been passed here and there. But what can be done? One must let people talk until their gray beards pass away <note>A German idiom suggesting that one should simply wait for critics to grow old and vanish, or that their opinions will eventually fade with time.</note>.

<margin>I have always judged it to be the mark of an illustrious and wise man to disregard the slanders of fools and the wicked with a great spirit. <note>original Latin: *Semper præclari & Sapientis hominis esse judicavi, stultorum & improborum calumnias magno animo parvifacere.*</note></margin>
But I also say and declare that everyone judges a thing according to how they understand it, and according to whether they are **favorably disposed** <note>original: *affectioniret*, from the Latin *affectionatus*, meaning to have a specific inclination or prejudice toward something.</note> either toward my person or toward the teachings of my aforementioned writings.

<margin>Though we cannot all compose, we all wish to judge. <note>Khunrath uses a rhyming German proverb: *Könne wir nicht alle dichten / so wollen wir doch alle richten.*</note> But a mind conscious of what is right laughs at the lies of rumor. <note>original Latin: *Sed, Conscia mens recti, famæ mendacia ridet.*</note></margin>
The fool judges foolishly; the ignorant, ignorantly; the merely worldly, quite worldly; the mocker, mockingly; he who is full of envy, spitefully; the slanderer, slanderously; the despiser, despicably; every bird sings according to how its beak has grown <note>A common German proverb meaning everyone speaks according to their own nature or ability.</note>. The world rewards in no other way. But be this as it may, I know for certain on the other hand—and can also prove it (if necessary) with many letters—that those skilled in the art, good

Only the person who is **DIVINELY** <note>original German: *GOTTweißlich*, literally "God-wisely," referring to wisdom derived from divine inspiration.</note> wise and learned, illuminated by the **LIGHT** of **NATURE** <note>The *Lumen Naturae* (Light of Nature) is a central concept in Renaissance alchemy and philosophy, referring to the innate knowledge of the physical and spiritual world granted by God to humanity through observation and reason.</note>, and who truly knows themselves, can draw conclusions that are **DIVINELY** wise, in accordance with nature, and Christian. No one else.

May **GOD** convert all righteous hearts that are capable of conversion, and grant them to recognize and accept the **LIGHT** of **TRUTH** in the Holy Biblical Scripture; in the Great World-Book of **NATURE**; and in themselves. This I wish them from the bottom of my heart. Otherwise, fie upon the Devil, as the supreme slanderer of the good and founder of all evil, along with all his stubborn students and scoundrels <note>original German: *Schüpen*, an archaic derogatory term for rogues or worthless individuals.</note>. <margin>The Author's Prophecy regarding his writings.</margin>
My **AMPHITHEATRUM**, this Philosophical **CONFESSION**, and others of my similar writings, although they are heavily contested, will indeed remain. **God** will, at all times, awaken good, sensible people who will help to honorably defend and represent them.

<margin>Truth is pressed, but not oppressed. And at last, a good cause triumphs. <note>original Latin: *Veritas premitur, non opprimitur. Et tandem bona causa triumphat.*</note></margin>

# PREFACE.

...have never yet made; I would otherwise surely distinguish myself with it and let it be seen. Oh, my dear friend, what are you saying? What do I hear? Dear fellow, wait just a while longer: before I paint more clearly before the noses of you and your like those brain-shaking fantasies <note>original German: *hirnschlotterende Phantasiẽ*; likely referring to shaky, ill-conceived ideas that rattle the mind or confuse the senses.</note> in this Art, and also give an account of each and every point to your liking—**FROM WHERE**, **WHEN**, and in **WHAT MANNER** or **WAY** I have thorough knowledge of that which I write. If there is but a tiny spark of the recognition of nature-accordant, Alchemical, Universal <note>original German: *Catholischer*; in this context, the term is used in its original sense of "universal" or "all-encompassing," referring to a truth that applies to the entire natural world.</note> Truth within you, then your own conscience will testify to me, against you, that I have not written falsely.

<term>Alchemy</term>: The ancient art and speculative philosophy aiming to achieve the transmutation of base metals into gold and the discovery of a universal cure.
<term>Magnalia</term>: Latin for "great things," referring here to the divine mysteries hidden in physical creation.
<term>Nature</term>: In this context, the living, divinely-ordered system that contains the secrets of transformation.
<term>Subject of the Stone</term>: The specific physical substance chosen by the alchemist to undergo the process of the "Great Work."
<term>Matter</term>: The raw material or *materia prima*.
<term>Philosophers</term>: Historically, this refers to alchemists or "natural philosophers" who studied the secrets of the physical and spiritual worlds.
<term>Analogy</term>: A comparison between two things, used by alchemists to describe their secret substances using common objects (like an egg).

<summary>This page explains that while the primary material of alchemy is known by many different names across various traditions, it remains a single, unified substance. The author notes that ancient sages used these many names and analogies to hide the "Great Works" of God from the mockery of the uninitiated.</summary>

# The Third Chapter.

<margin>What Nature is.</margin>
Firstly, **NATURE** is a supremely wise, self-moving, life-giving, exceedingly powerful, and miraculous **LIGHT** and **FIRE**—indeed, a powerfully strong spirit, or spiritual force—flowing forth from the all-wise, eternal, living, almighty, and wondrous triune <margin>a Deuteronomy 9:3. b John 4:24. 1 Corinthians 3:17.</margin> **GOD** (who is a fire [a] and a spirit [b]) Himself. This force enters into the Hyleatic <term>Hyleatic: from the Greek *hyle*, referring to the raw matter or "stuff" of the universe</term>—that is, the primordial <note>original: *Pri-materialische*</note> watery **CHAOS**—which was created at the very beginning of the world. It blesses and also impregnates that chaos, sustaining the entire structure of the Great World <note>The "Great World" refers to the Macrocosm, or the universe, as opposed to the "Little World" or Microcosm of the human being.</note> built from it, until the end appointed for it by **GOD**.

Just as the devil disguises himself as an angel of light and causes great harm, so too do the alchemists disguise common mercury as the Mercury of the Philosophers ☿, and in this way they achieve nothing good.
</margin>

...knows (God be praised) their tricks. Here, there will be no substitution <note>original Latin: *quid pro quo*</note>, nor "dung for balsam" <note>original Latin: *merda pro balsamo*; a common alchemical expression for mistaking a worthless substance for a precious one.</note>. The Philosophers speak unanimously: **"Our mercury ☿ is not the mercury of the common people"** <note>original Latin: *Noster ☿ non est ☿ vulgi*</note>; our ☿ is not the common ☿—that is, quicksilver. If then quicksilver is the common ☿, how can it then be the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>original Latin: *☿ Philosophorum*</note> and the universal philosophical master-key of the metals? Oho! The **Mercury of the Wise** <note>original Latin: *☿ Sophorum*</note> is a far different thing than quicksilver, or something taken out of and from the same. All who have worked in this way have been miserably led astray and unspeakably, shamefully lost. That all true Philosophers held common quicksilver to be of no value at all in this matter is found clearly enough in their authentic books.

<margin>
HERMES says in chapter 2: "O blessed watery, sea-like form" <note>original Latin: *ô benedicta forma aquina, pontica*</note>, not "quicksilver-like" <note>original Latin: *Hydrargyrica*</note>, "by which you dissolve the elements" <note>original Latin: *qua Elementa dissolvis*</note>:
</margin>

**"And many are deceived in working with that common quicksilver,"** <note>original Latin: *Et multi sunt decepti in operando in illo argento vivo vulgi*</note> says the Great *Rosarium* <note>The *Rosarium Philosophorum* (Rose Garden of the Philosophers) is a seminal 16th-century alchemical text.</note>.

# Chapter IX.

At one time, a person produced rich silver samples from verdigris <note>A green pigment or crust formed on copper; alchemists often experimented with it as a source of copper "seed."</note>. Upon proper investigation, it was discovered that he had obtained a certain *aqua fortis* <note>original: "Aqua fort"; literally "strong water," the historical name for nitric acid.</note> which he needed for the work, in which (unbeknownst to him) silver had already been dissolved <note>original: "solviret"</note>; the bottle had been accidentally switched by another person. 

Yet the good man—even after the error had been pointed out to him—would have let himself be burned at the stake <note>A German idiom (sich verbrennen lassen) meaning he would have staked his life on his claim.</note> swearing that he had created that silver through his supposed **Particular Art** <term>Particular Art</term> <note>In alchemy, a "Particular" refers to a process that produces a specific result or a small amount of precious metal, as opposed to the "Universal" work of the Philosopher's Stone which transforms everything.</note> by way of transformation. 

Had his arts, or yours, proceeded from a true, natural foundation, you would have been able to replicate the results and continue working with profit. There are many such examples to tell, but it is unnecessary to report every one specifically <note>original: "specialiter"</note>, as it would be far too long-winded.

**SUMMARY:** As long as these simple people, who do not understand **NATURE**, take silver- or gold-bearing **MA-** <note>The word is cut off by the page break; the catchword suggests it continues as "MATERIA" or "materials."</note>

### Chapter IX.

<margin>CONSTELLATIONS</margin>
You also cannot excuse yourself with **TIME**, claiming that the correct **Constellations** <note>original: "Constellationes"</note> and heavenly influences belonging to the task are now lacking to you, and that the heavens do not now work as they perhaps did that one time. For the Philosopher <margin>a In *The Lily*.</margin> <note>original: "In Lilio"; likely referring to the *Lilium Alchimiae*, a text often attributed to Arnaldus de Villa Nova.</note> expressly says: *That the WORK is not caused by the movement of the celestial bodies, because it can be done at all times* <note>original: "Quod OPUS non causetur à motu Superiorum, quia omni tempore fieri potest"</note>; that the **Work** is not caused by the course of the heavens and the stars, since it can be made at each and every time. On the contrary, my **slanderers** <note>original: *Calumnianten*</note>—to whom I (just like the honest people I mentioned) have recounted such **"fine little tricks"** (which we and other good people have experienced *passively* <note>original: *passivè*</note> and not *actively* <note>original: *activè*</note>) by way of my profession and office, as a caution and heartfelt warning—ought to watch themselves well, 
<margin>*It is not the knowledge of evil, but the use of evil that condemns. For there is one kind of knowledge for recognition, and another for approval.* <note>original: *Non scientia mali, sed usus mali damnat. Est enim scientia alia Cognitionis, alia approbationis.*</note></margin>
either to desist from such things, or at least not to become such fellows themselves, nor to fall into the **rogues' guild** <note>original: *Schelmenzunfft*</note> of those who carry out the tricks I have told, or other similar, no better deeds in other matters; because some of them [many...]

<meta>Sig: Hh ij; catchword: viel (many)</meta>

<summary>The author uses historical and social examples, such as the Spartans and fashion critics, to argue that exposing vice is a method of moral education. He distinguishes between knowing a crime to warn others (passive knowledge) and practicing a crime (active use).</summary>
<keywords>Spartans, drunkards, fashion controversy, Pluderhosen, slander, passive vs active knowledge, moral philosophy, rogues' guild</keywords>

He previously stated that knowing about evil is not the same as practicing it, and that his exposure of alchemical fraud is a public service. He concludes the sentence from the previous page by suggesting that his critics might be naturally inclined toward the very roguery they accuse him of.</meta>

->Trewherzige<-

...perhaps, in an assumed manner, might be quite inclined and disposed toward it.

<margin>
**Ingratitude** is the greatest vice.
</margin>

Regarding the reproach made by the wicked and alchemical, intentionally-deceitful guild of **gold-fraudsters** <term>gold-fraudsters <note>original: *Gold-Keser*; a derogatory term for those who fake gold or cheat in alchemical transactions</note></term>, because of the publication of their most useful secret **tricks** <note>original: *Handgriffe*</note> and very quick **practices** <note>original: *practicen*</note>: we grant and wish that, since they cannot know much, they may keep these things to themselves. Instead, I expect a different reward from honest, good people who can save a great deal of money through my guidance. To these people, I give my proper and heartfelt thanks.

<margin>
One can nevertheless learn good **techniques** <note>original: *Handgriffe*</note> from good artists; it would not be good if the deceivers alone were able to **work** <note>original: *laboriren*</note>.
</margin>

As for those others, I leave them this in return as a final **reward** <note>original: *remuneration*</note>: namely, that all **students of nature** <note>original: *Naturkündiger*</note>, lovers of art, and otherwise honest people shall have a horror and loathing of them, such that they are held as nothing other than **foul-smelling** <note>original: *vbelstinckende*</note> and rotten carcasses. Every—

<meta>catchword: man</meta>

<summary>The author dismisses the complaints of fraudulent alchemists who are angry that he has exposed their secret tricks. He argues that honest people will benefit from his warnings, while the fraudsters deserve to be treated as social outcasts.</summary>
<keywords>alchemy, fraud, Gold-Keser, manual techniques, ethics, students of nature, social reputation</keywords>

**Warning.**

<margin>
For a **wolfish** roast, one needs a **dogged** <gloss>dog-like</gloss> jelly <note>original: *Auff einen Wölffenen Braten / hört ein gehundene Sülze*; a proverb meaning that a harsh person deserves a harsh response, or "tit for tat."</note>.
</margin>
man, whenever one sees one of them, should spit upon him and say: "Fie on you, you deceitful **gold-maker**!" <note>original: *Goldmacher*; a derogatory term here for alchemical charlatans.</note>
